results.title: How to Engage with Hard-to-Reach or Marginalized Community Groups
results.content: # What are some of the best practices for engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups? Engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups is a crucial part of community consultation. In this article, we will share some of the best practices for engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups, based on our experience and research. Before you start engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups, you need to identify who they are, where they are, and what their interests and concerns are. Before engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups, it's essential to identify and understand them thoroughly. This approach ensures tailored and respectful engagement with marginalized communities. Use detailed data sources like census reports, local surveys, and community feedback to drill down into the specifics of who these groups are and what makes them tick. Be sure that the benefit of engagement is clearly understood and communicated in the currency of the people you want to reach, and make ambassadors of those who are trusted and beloved by the community. Once you have identified and understood your target groups, you need to choose the most appropriate methods and tools to engage with them. Another challenge of engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups is recruiting and incentivizing participants. To further improve recruitment and incentivization, focus on building trust through partnerships with community leaders or organizations that already have established credibility with your target groups. Using community spaces that are close by, Shine UCA, Heart Centre, St Vincent's Conduct a thorough assessment of the community's needs and priorities so projects are relevant and meaningful Engage with stakeholders to ensure we align with existing projects, are inclusive and responsive to diverse needs. Building a community from the ground-up approach Continuously monitor engagement and gather feedback All activities and projects led by the needs of the individuals Effective communication. After you have facilitated and supported participation, you need to analyze and report your findings from your engagement with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups. The final step of engaging with hard-to-reach or marginalized community groups is to follow up and evaluate the impact of your engagement. * How do you keep yourself motivated and engaged in community consultation?

results.title: Enrollment of Participants From Marginalized Racial and Ethnic Groups: A Comparative Assessment of the STEADY-PD III and SURE-PD3 Trials - PMC
results.content: Two large phase 3 randomized clinical trials sponsored by the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), STEADY-PD III and SURE-PD3, screened participants from overlapping Parkinson Study Group clinical sites under similar eligibility criteria but differed in participation by underrepresented minorities. Although both trials targeted similar participants, STEADY-PD III was able to consent and recruit a higher percentage of patients from racial and ethnic marginalized groups. Recruitment into randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in neurology is often challenging due to complexities in protocol design.4 Recruitment of participants belonging to marginalized racial and ethnic groups has been low in several National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)-funded and other clinical trials evaluating a broad range of neurologic conditions, including movement disorders.5,6 In the case of PD, representation of such patients in clinical trials has historically fallen below their proportional prevalence, lessening the generalizability of therapeutics development for individuals with PD.7. In this study, we compare the different recruitment efforts and enrollment of persons from marginalized racial and ethnic groups in STEADY-PD III and SURE-PD3 trials to understand how their differences may inform efforts to improve inclusivity of future trials and observational studies. Despite recruiting participants over similar time periods, under similar eligibility criteria and from similar sites (including geographic location), STEADY-PD III was able to successfully enroll more participants belonging to marginalized racial and ethnic groups when compared with SURE-PD3. The increase in community physicians' engagement in clinical trials and the selection of coordinators strongly connected to the community did not result in higher enrollment of patients from marginalized racial and ethnic groups.26 The RECRUIT trial reported that promoting trust-based approaches between physician-investigators and minority-serving physicians and their patients might be a successful strategy.27 This intervention was implemented in the STEADY-PD III trial at selected sites. Fox Foundation was created with a goal of developing specific interventions to educate and engage participants belonging to marginalized racial and ethnic groups in PD research.28 Of note, only 6 clinical sites requested additional funds to enhance racial and ethnic diversity in enrollment in STEADY-PD III, and none did in SURE-PD3. STEADY-PD III enrolled a larger percentage of participants belonging to marginalized racial and ethnic groups compared with SURE-PD3, although both trials targeted similar PD subpopulations and recruited from overlapping clinical sites.

results.title: Understanding Terrorist Recruitment Tactics in Modern Conflicts
results.content: Recruitment initiatives often target individuals through ideological appeals and social networks, capitalizing on factors such as disenfranchisement and identity crises. * Social Networks and Peer Influence * Target Demographics in Terrorist Recruitment * Case Studies of Notable Recruitment Tactics * Media’s Role in Facilitating Recruitment * The Evolving Landscape of Recruitment Tactics * Implications for Counter-Terrorism Strategies Terrorist recruitment tactics encompass various methods employed by extremist organizations to attract and enlist members. This ideological appeal resonates with individuals seeking purpose or belonging, making it an effective tool for recruitment. Understanding these ideological recruitment tactics is vital for developing effective counter-terrorism strategies. Social Networks and Peer Influence Social networks and peer influence significantly shape the recruitment tactics employed by terrorist organizations. As a result, terrorist organizations can efficiently recruit new members through the manipulation of existing social networks, making targeted outreach an effective recruitment tactic. By understanding how social networks and peer influence operate within terrorist recruitment tactics, counter-terrorism strategies can be better developed. By fostering social inclusion and economic opportunities, and promoting community engagement, it is possible to mitigate the impact of terrorist recruitment tactics targeting marginalized groups. ### Al-Qaeda Al-Qaeda employs a variety of sophisticated recruitment tactics aimed at attracting individuals to its extremist ideology. Community resilience strategies are vital in countering terrorist recruitment efforts. Together, they can implement tailored programs that directly address the motivations behind terrorist recruitment tactics, ultimately reducing the appeal of extremist groups. ### Community Resilience Strategies Community resilience strategies focus on strengthening social cohesion and empowering local communities to deter terrorist recruitment tactics. By enhancing community resilience, the appeal of terrorist recruitment tactics can be significantly diminished, thereby fostering a safer and more united society. These initiatives encompass a range of activities, including intelligence sharing, community engagement, and targeted operations against individuals and groups involved in recruitment. Notable changes in recruitment tactics include the rise of online communities where individuals can discuss ideology and share experiences. Understanding the evolving landscape of recruitment tactics is crucial for developing effective counter-terrorism strategies. results.title: Participation of Marginalized Groups
results.content: Pro Peace | Frieden braucht Fachleute ## Suche # Participation of Marginalized Groups Making sure that everybody is heard and can participate is an essential element of **sustainable peace processes**. All affected parties in a conflict need to be able to express their needs and interests and be taken into serious consideration in order to come to an agreement that everybody will accept, respect, and support. Unfortunately, peace agreements are more often rather exclusive. The interests of less powerful, marginalized groups, like women, youth, or Indigenous Peoples are generally not taken into account. To achieve inclusive peace processes, **we connect actors and stakeholders** vertically and horizontally. First, horizontal connections among organizations, institutions, and individuals who are working for the same goals or face the same challenges are strengthened. With mutual support and coordinated activities, they can create a critical mass to put their issues on the peace table. Then, vertically, we link grassroots, civil society and peace organizations to high level decision makers. We organize dialogues and community meetings, providing **safe space for exchange** among the various stakeholders of the peace process. Thereby we enable a flow of information in which participants receive direct updates on the dynamics of the peace process, discuss concerns and think about common solutions. In addition, a weekly radio program builds a bridge between people from remote conflict areas, and experts and decision makers. The radio is a two-way line: on the one hand informing about the peace process and on the other providing space for discussing the concerns of the listeners. ## The Kutawato Multimedia Network (KuMuNet) ## Engagement with Senior High Schools ## Discussing Peace
